rewrites.title: Degron-based separation of establishment and maintenance
rewrites.description: Use an acute degron (dTAG/AID) on JUN/FOS family members and degrade them only after priming but before re-challenge. If memory persists without AP-1 protein, it is stored elsewhere. If it is lost, AP-1 is needed for maintenance, not just establishment.

rewrites.title: Footprinting and chromatin profiling in natural in vivo injury/inflammation models
rewrites.description: Profile cells from tissues after resolved natural perturbations (e.g., skin wounding, inflammation, or aged vs. young tissue) using ATAC-seq, CUT&RUN for JUN/FOS, and Hi-C or HiChIP, and compare with matched naive tissue. Persistent AP-1 motif footprints, retained enhancer-promoter loops, and faster re-induction of target genes on a second injury, correlated with the motif-containing regions opened by the first event, would support AP-1-dependent memory under physiological conditions without genetic manipulation.

rewrites.title: Synthetic minimal AP-1 memory circuit with tunable hysteresis
rewrites.description: In a cell type with little endogenous AP-1 activity, build an orthogonal bZIP (AP-1 leucine zipper fused to a non-native DNA-binding domain) driving a synthetic enhancer array in which motif number, spacing, and feedback strength are systematically varied, and drive it transiently with a small-molecule or light input. Measure the hysteresis width and bistability boundary of the resulting input-output curves to determine whether AP-1's autoregulatory architecture is by itself sufficient to store a stable state, and which design parameters set memory duration.

rewrites.title: Feedback-network perturbation and model fitting
rewrites.description: Build an ODE model of AP-1 with positive autoregulation (the JUN promoter has AP-1 sites) and chromatin-state variables, fit it to dose and time-course data, and predict the effect of breaking the loop. Test the predictions by CRISPR mutation of AP-1 sites at the JUN/FOS loci and optogenetic pulsing of AP-1 factors, looking for loss of the persistent state when the feedback is cut.

rewrites.title: Dose titration of memory erasure
rewrites.description: Test how much perturbation is needed to erase memory by dose-titrating inhibitors of chromatin remodeling (BRG1/SWI-SNF), histone acetyltransferases, or DNA replication/cell division, and measure when the primed response reverts to the naive state. If memory decays only with disruption of AP-1-dependent chromatin and not with loss of AP-1 protein levels, chromatin structure rather than ongoing AP-1 activity carries the memory.

rewrites.title: Long-term chromatin accessibility tracking after a transient stimulus
rewrites.description: Expose cells to a defined, transient AP-1-activating stimulus (e.g., TPA, growth factor, injury signal), then perform time-resolved ATAC-seq and CUT&RUN for FOS/JUN and H3K27ac after washout (days to weeks, across cell divisions). Persistence of AP-1-motif-enriched accessible sites, and of AP-1 binding at them, after the stimulus is gone would indicate a memory state.

rewrites.title: Stimulus re-exposure (recall) assay
rewrites.description: Apply a priming stimulus (e.g., a short TNF or growth-factor pulse), allow a rest period, then re-stimulate and compare the magnitude and kinetics of AP-1 target gene induction (RNA-seq, nascent transcription via PRO-seq) with naive cells. Faster or stronger responses on re-challenge, lost when AP-1 binding sites are mutated or AP-1 is degraded during the rest period, would demonstrate functional memory.

rewrites.title: Stimulus-history dependence with a live reporter
rewrites.description: Vary the timing, duration, and frequency of stimuli while imaging a live AP-1-responsive reporter in single cells. Hysteresis or history-dependent thresholds that match a fitted bistable model would show that AP-1 encodes past input rather than just reporting the current signal.

rewrites.title: Mitotic retention and single-molecule residence time in primed cells
rewrites.description: Image Halo-tagged JUN/FOS retention on mitotic chromosomes (with mitotic CUT&RUN as the genomic counterpart) and use single-molecule tracking of bound fraction and residence time in naive versus primed cells. Longer residence or mitotic retention in primed cells would indicate a mechanism for heritability, whereas unchanged kinetics would point to chromatin or cofactors instead.

rewrites.title: Live imaging of AP-1 binding through mitosis
rewrites.description: Use endogenous HaloTag-tagged FOS or JUN and live single-molecule or time-lapse imaging to determine which AP-1 sites remain bound on mitotic chromosomes. Then test whether daughter cells that inherit bound sites reactivate target genes faster than those that do not.

rewrites.title: Dose-threshold comparison with optogenetic AP-1 induction
rewrites.description: Finely titrate the stimulus to locate the sharp threshold at which AP-1 enhancer priming switches on, then compare cells just below versus just above the threshold (sorted on a live AP-1 reporter) for long-term recall. In addition, induce FOS/JUN optogenetically without the original stimulus, to alter AP-1 activity by a route that bypasses other stimulus-induced changes.

rewrites.title: Barcoded lineage tracing of memory heterogeneity
rewrites.description: Introduce lineage barcodes and a fluorescent AP-1 target reporter, then stimulate cells and follow clonal lineages over several divisions. Comparing memory between sister and unrelated clones shows whether memory is cell-autonomous, inherited, and bistable, or a graded, population-level effect.

rewrites.title: Heritability analysis across lineage trees
rewrites.description: Combine live imaging of an AP-1 activity reporter with expressed lineage barcodes so that each cell's state can be placed on a family tree, then compute intraclass correlation of AP-1 activity and of AP-1-dependent target expression between sisters, cousins, and increasingly distant relatives. Fitting the decay of correlation with generation number gives a memory half-life in cell divisions, and the analysis can be repeated under AP-1 degradation to ask whether AP-1 carries the inherited state or merely correlates with it.

rewrites.title: Chromatin persistence after AP-1 withdrawal
rewrites.description: Use a degron-tagged JUN or FOS that can be switched on for a short pulse and then removed within minutes, and track chromatin accessibility (ATAC-seq), H3K27ac, and AP-1 occupancy (CUT&Tag) at primed enhancers over days to weeks. If the enhancer state outlasts AP-1 binding, that supports a self-sustaining memory rather than one dependent on ongoing transcription factor activity.

rewrites.title: Open-loop clamp of AP-1 expression
rewrites.description: Delete or mutate the AP-1 binding sites in the FOS/JUN promoters and re-supply the subunits from a tunable exogenous promoter titrated to match wild-type mean protein level. Loss of the heritable state despite identical average AP-1 activity would localize memory to the trans autoregulatory feedback loop rather than to the chromatin that AP-1 binds.

rewrites.title: Prime, washout, and restimulate with acute AP-1 removal
rewrites.description: Prime cells with a stimulus, wash out, then acutely degrade (dTAG/AID) c-Jun/Fos or express A-Fos either before or after the rest period, and measure the faster or stronger secondary response. If memory persists after AP-1 removal, AP-1 is only the initiator. If memory requires AP-1 during the rest period or at recall, AP-1 is needed for maintenance.

rewrites.title: Synthetic AP-1 motif-array library for minimal sufficient memory encoding
rewrites.description: Integrate at one fixed safe-harbor site a library of synthetic loci varying AP-1 motif number, affinity, spacing, flanking nucleosome-positioning sequence, and core promoter, then deliver a standardized AP-1 pulse and assay which configurations remain active days later. This tests whether AP-1 sites alone suffice to build a memory element and identifies the sequence features that convert transient binding into a persistent state.

rewrites.title: Synthetic AP-1 site array for sufficiency
rewrites.description: Integrate arrays of AP-1 motifs (and motif-scrambled controls) at a neutral genomic locus adjacent to a reporter, then drive AP-1 binding transiently with an optogenetic or chemically inducible Fos/Jun module. Persistent reporter expression and accessibility after induction ends would show that AP-1 binding is sufficient to write a heritable state, independent of pre-existing locus context.

rewrites.title: Acute AP-1 degron with long-term memory readout
rewrites.description: Using endogenous dTAG/AID degrons on FOS, JUN and ATF family members, degrade AP-1 at defined times after a transient stimulus (e.g., TNF, wounding, or neuronal activity). Then track whether the induced chromatin and transcriptional state persists for weeks after AP-1 loss, which distinguishes a state that AP-1 initiates from one that AP-1 must keep maintaining.

rewrites.title: Dose-and-interval mapping of memory decay in single cells
rewrites.description: Systematically vary stimulus strength, duration, and the gap before re-stimulation, reading out per-cell response amplitude and AP-1 site accessibility. Fitting the resulting surface tests whether the system behaves like a bistable switch, a slowly decaying analog trace, or simple residual protein.
